prompt: Two boxes have the same outside dimensions, but one has much thicker walls. Explain why comparing their external size is insufficient to compare their storage capacity. A response of around 80 words is enough.
text: Storage capacity depends on a box’s internal dimensions, not its external size. Although the two boxes occupy the same amount of space outside, thicker walls take up more of that space, leaving less room inside for storage. For a rectangular box, capacity is calculated by multiplying its internal length, width, and height. Therefore, assuming otherwise similar construction, the box with thicker walls has a smaller capacity. Comparing external dimensions alone ignores the space occupied by the walls and base.
